decisive_moments.reason: Pro directly addressed the strongest objection—unknown distribution shifts and lifecycle adaptability—by incorporating adversarial, shift, safety, and lifecycle evaluations while retaining a conditional path to larger models.

Con correctly identified the epistemic limit of finite evaluations and explained why capability can function as a reliability resource, but did not establish why that should defeat a smallest-passing default.

Pro clearly framed the dispute as evidence-based minimization versus speculative headroom, while explicitly preserving developer freedom when larger-model benefits are tied to workload-specific consequences.

Con ultimately accepted nearly all of the conjecture's operational content, including that the smallest passing model is the strongest default and that larger models require evidence-based justification.

flags.quote: larger ... increases ... operational complexity, and often the blast radius of failures
Larger models may provide valuable robustness, better generalization, and safer graceful degradation
